## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c45a761382f8f4497c2c6f1992d4ce1875356d24`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #12220 (body and its four comments: triage 6121883932, claim 6122095115, os-dev-report 6122833717, ACCEPT 6122895898), PR #12231 (body, the 12-file list, the net diff against `main` at the head, +863/-34), and the 42 check-runs on the head. Files at the head were read through the contents API only to confirm what the diff implies about each package's `exports` map. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Published surface of `@object-ui/react`. The entry `src/index.ts` re-exports `./context/index.js`, which re-exports `./InlineEditContext.js`, so every export of that file reaches the package's one `exports` entry `.`:

1. New runtime export `resolveApprovalLock(input)` — right. It is the one rule triage asked for ("one rule, not two copies"): both sites call it, and neither keeps a copy of the column read (at the head the only `approval_status` reads left in `DetailView.tsx` and `RecordDetailView.tsx` are the `recordStatus` argument of each call, plus comments). Its home is right: `@object-ui/react` is a `dependency` of app-shell and a `peerDependency` of plugin-detail, and it owns `InlineEditContextValue`, whose `locked` / `approvalPending` / `approvalReadAnswered` fields the rule interprets.
2. New type exports `ApprovalLockInput` and `ApprovalLockState` — right. A public function's argument and result have to be spellable by its callers.
3. `InlineEditContextValue.approvalReadAnswered?: boolean` (optional) — right, widening. The provider always supplies it (default `false`), and a hand-built context value is not broken.
4. `InlineEditProviderProps.approvalReadAnswered?: boolean`, default `false` — right, a widening of the accept-set. Omitted, the behaviour is the pre-PR one (item 7).
5. Nothing removed, renamed or narrowed on this entry — right, checked against the diff and the entry files at the head.

6. Accept-set of the rule — right. Three ordered branches: an `openApproval` decides (`pending: true`, `locked` per the node's `lockRecord`); otherwise `readAnswered` means `pending: false, locked: false`; otherwise the column stands in with the unchanged vocabulary (`pending`, `in_approval`), read as pending AND locked. `recordStatus: unknown` is the right type for a value read off a record.

7. `@object-ui/plugin-detail` `DetailView`, the `showHeader === false` band — right. It maps the host pair to `openApproval: hostPending || hostLocked ? { locked: hostLocked } : null`. With `approvalReadAnswered` absent or `false`, all four combinations of host `locked` / `approvalPending` reproduce the removed OR-chain: `false/false` falls to the column; `false/true` reads pending and editable (objectui#2902); `true/true` and `true/false` read pending and locked (objectui#2618, a host `locked` still counts as an approval, as it did before). I checked each combination against the removed lines. The only new outcome is `readAnswered: true` with `false/false`: no band, no lock, no Recall lever, which is the card's expected answer. `DetailViewProps` and the entry `index.tsx` are untouched, so plugin-detail publishes no surface change — right.

8. `@object-ui/app-shell` `RecordDetailView` — right. With `answered: false` the call reproduces the removed two lines over every combination of `pendingRequest` and column value. With `answered: true` and no request the page threads `locked: false` / `approvalPending: false`, and the header Edit, the body pencils and `InlineEditSaveBar` (which consumes the same `approvalLocked`) unlock together. `approvalReadAnswered={approvals.answered}` is threaded on the page's one `InlineEditProvider`, so the band under `record:details` (which builds its `DetailView` with `showHeader: schema.showHeader ?? false` and `inlineEdit` on) reads the same flag the page read. `approvalIsSubmitter` still reads the pending request only.

9. `useRecordApprovals` gains `answered` — right, and internal: neither the hook nor `UseRecordApprovalsResult` is on the app-shell entry (`src/index.ts` and `hooks/index.ts` at the head), so no app-shell export moves. `answered` is `true` only when `answeredFor` equals the current `[objectName, recordId]` key; a 404 / 501 clears it and sets `available: false`; any other failure keeps the last state, so a transient error after an answer keeps `true` and a first-read failure stays `false`. `available` is left as it was, which the claim asked for.

10. Fixture triage in `RecordDetailView.approvalRecallGate.test.tsx` (the "no request to consult" pin) and in the `approvalLocked composition` block of `RecordDetailView.userActionPredicates.test.tsx` — right. Both pins are about a backend with no approvals API; an empty 200 is now an answered read, so they answer the list route 404, which is the backend their own comments describe. The predicates file keeps its top-level `afterEach(vi.unstubAllGlobals)`, so the block-scoped stub does not leak. The new header-Edit pin waits for the enabled state, which is the measurement.

11. New pins at all four layers (rule, hook, page, band), each carrying the three triage pins and the `lockRecord: false` control; the band's absence pin is paired with a same-record control that renders the band — right.

12. `packages/plugin-detail/README.md` bullet — right: prose, no import; `README Export Check` on the head is success.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/12220-approval-lock-follows-request.md`: `@object-ui/react` `minor`, `@object-ui/app-shell` `patch`, `@object-ui/plugin-detail` `patch`. This matches what the diff publishes: react widens its entry (① items 1 to 4); the other two change behaviour only (① items 7 to 9). Not `skip-changeset`, and no `major` (objectui's fixed group never declares one). `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Claim Re-read` and `Changeset Overwrite Report` are all success on the head.

`Clause-②:` line — the PR body reads `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; right. `yes` takes at least `minor`, which react carries, and `(widening)` is the one arm a pure addition may take. The claim declared `Clause-②: no` with the seat to re-state it at ACCEPT if the shared rule added a published export or field; it did, and the ACCEPT re-stated it. The changeset body names every added export and the optional prop and states that nothing is removed or renamed, so a consumer reading `CHANGELOG.md` sees the whole widening.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared.

`deviations` (os-dev-report 6122833717), each answered:

1. Two existing test files and the README outside the claim's file surface — right. The fixture edits are forced by the change (an empty 200 no longer stands for "no approvals API"); the README bullet documents the new prop. The claim's serial-constraints read names no in-flight neighbour on these files.
2. `useRecordApprovals.ts` changed — right. The claim allowed it once `available` was measured unable to tell a 2xx from an in-flight or failed read, and the hook at the head shows exactly that (`available` starts `true` and is set `false` only on 404 / 501). The header-comment amendment matches the behaviour.
3. react `minor`, Clause-② re-stated at ACCEPT — right; see ②.
4. Commit trailers use the model-free pair — right by rule: objectui AGENTS.md prescribes exactly that pair, and the harness reminder's own precedence clause defers to repo instructions. The ACCEPT comment reads the trailers and body as carrying no model identifier; the commits themselves are outside this brief's inputs and were not re-read.
5. Worktree base 6c437b0 against the dispatch's 803f678; the PR's `mergeable_state` is `behind` — not a veto: the queue rebases, and no hunk on the file list meets objectui#12194's `ManagedByBadge` hunk.
6. `check:readme-exports` NOT MEASURED locally — answered by the head's `README Export Check`: success.

`out_of_scope_findings`, each answered:

1. On a record switch `useRecordApprovals` keeps the previous record's `requests` until the new read lands — pre-existing (the hook's effect clears `requests` only when the key is falsy), inferred from reading and not reproduced, so under Prime Directive #10 it is a note, not a filing; the ACCEPT record is its carrier. Reviewer's adjacent reading, same shape: two reads in flight can land out of order, and a late answer for the previous record then overwrites `requests` and `answeredFor`; the page shows the previous record's open request (pre-existing) or, with none, falls to the column, which is what the removed code did too. The new field adds no wrong answer there. Noted, not filed; same carrier.
2. The fallback reads the literal `approval_status`, not the flow's declared `approvalStatusField` — triage's direction did not include it; the dev measured the field unreachable from the console (the approvals row carries `lock_record` and no field name; the record page reads no flow metadata); after this PR the column is read only while no read has answered. The PR body (H5) and the ACCEPT carry it. Nothing to escalate.

Dispatch reading the dev called ("H1 (c), my call"): a first read that fails 5xx or on the network, and a read still in flight, are not an answer, so the column locks for that window — right. It is fail-closed and identical to the pre-PR behaviour for that window; the alternative (unlock while nothing is known) would flash a record with a real request editable. Pinned at the hook (cases (c) and in flight).

Governance: the 12 paths touch no governed surface; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is success and the dev's `check-governed-queue-guard --test` read NOT GOVERNED.

Check-runs on the head, as read when this record was finalised: 43 total; 40 success; 3 skipped by design (`dependabot`, `Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard)`); 0 in progress; 0 failure. All eight `Test (shard n/8)` runs and the `Test` aggregate, `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Build & E2E`, `Test (dist pins)`, `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `README Export Check`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and the whole changeset family are success. An earlier reading during this review had six shards still `in_progress`; they converged to success before the record was posted.
